name: Wen T’ing-yün
bio: Wen T'ing-yün (Wen Tingyun) was a poet of the late T'ang dynasty, dated by Ayscough and Lowell's Contents to circa A.D. 850, and is known above all for lyrics written to popular tunes.
The archive holds one lyric from Fir-Flower Tablets (1921), a woman watching the river for a boat that does not come, written to the air "Looking South over the River and Dreaming".

poems.title: Sung to the Air: "Looking South Over the River and Dreaming"
poems.author: Wen T’ing-yün
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
The hair is combed,
The face is washed,
All is done.

Alone, in the upper story of my Summer-house, I bend forward, looking at the river.
A thousand sails pass--but among all of them the one is not.
The slant sunlight will not speak,
It will not speak.
The long-stretched water scarcely moves.

My bowels are broken within me.
Oh! Island of the White Water Flowers!
